reconstructed_theorem_text: For every real inner-product space E, equipped with its compatible norm, every function f from E to the real numbers, every nonnegative real number G, and every pair of vectors x and g in E, the following implication holds. Suppose that f is globally G-Lipschitz, meaning that |f(u) - f(v)| <= G * ||u - v|| for every u and v in E. Suppose also that g supports f at x on the whole space, meaning that f(x) + <g, y - x> <= f(y) for every y in E, where <.,.> is the real inner product. Then ||g|| <= G. Neither completeness nor finite dimensionality of E is required, and G = 0 is permitted.
objects: The normed additive commutative group E with a real inner-product-space structure; a real-valued function f; a nonnegative real Lipschitz bound G; a point x; and a supporting vector g.
domains: E is an arbitrary real inner-product space with its compatible norm, without completeness, finite-dimensionality, or nontriviality requirements. The domain and codomain of f are E and R, respectively. G belongs to the nonnegative real numbers [0, infinity). Both x and g belong to E. Inner products and all scalar inequalities are real-valued.
quantifiers: Universally quantify E and its stated structures, f: E -> R, G in [0, infinity), and x,g in E. The Lipschitz hypothesis universally quantifies u,v in E. The supporting inequality universally quantifies y in E. Under these hypotheses, conclude the norm bound for the given g. There is no existentially quantified point, vector, optimizer, or constant.
assumptions: For every u,v in E, |f(u) - f(v)| <= G * ||u - v||. For every y in E, f(x) + <g, y - x> <= f(y). These are global function inequalities. No separate assumption of convexity, differentiability, minimizer existence, or minimality of G is present.
conclusion: The norm of the supporting vector satisfies ||g|| <= G.
scopes: The single fixed G bounds f on all of E. The support condition is at the specified x and holds against every y in E, not merely nearby y or an optimizer. The conclusion concerns any g satisfying that condition; it does not assert that such a g exists. The endpoints G = 0 and g = 0 are allowed. No iteration index, horizon, or finite sum occurs in this statement.
constant_dependencies: G is arbitrary supplied data and need only be a valid nonnegative global Lipschitz bound, not the smallest such bound. The conclusion uses exactly G with coefficient 1 and introduces no hidden constant or dimension-dependent factor. It holds uniformly over all permissible E, f, x, and g.
